summary: Capcom's cooperative hunting-action franchise, spanning numbered console games, PSP/3DS/Switch portable entries, Stories RPG spin-offs, online/mobile services, and current-generation releases.

entries.title: Monster Hunter

emulation.notes: Use a legally dumped PS2 copy; online service features are archival/historical.

primary.why: The first Monster Hunter shipped for PlayStation 2; later G/Freedom versions are tracked as separate enhanced entries.
primary.how_to_play: Play a PS2 copy, or use PCSX2 with a legally dumped copy for higher output resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: Use Monster Hunter G/Freedom entries for enhanced versions rather than conflating them with the original.

entries.title: Monster Hunter G

emulation.notes: Use a legally dumped Wii copy.

primary.why: Monster Hunter G is the enhanced version of the original game; the Wii port is the later official release and the best fidelity route for this entry.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Wii version, or use Dolphin with a legally dumped copy.

entries.remaster_caveats: Japan/Korea-focused enhanced version; Monster Hunter Freedom is a separate PSP adaptation.

emulation.notes: Use a legally dumped PSP copy for high internal resolution.

primary.why: Freedom is the international PSP adaptation of Monster Hunter G and the only release route for this portable entry.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PSP or use PPSSPP with a legally dumped copy.

entries.title: Monster Hunter i

emulation.notes: Treat as preservation-only until a reliable mobile preservation route is sourced.

primary.why: Monster Hunter i is sourced as a DoCoMo phone port of Monster Hunter G, so the original Japanese mobile release is the only known route.
primary.how_to_play: Preservation-only: use original compatible Japanese mobile hardware/service data where legally available.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster or storefront route.

entries.title: Monster Hunter 2

emulation.notes: Use a legally dumped Japanese PS2 copy.

primary.why: Monster Hunter 2 was released exclusively in Japan for PlayStation 2.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese PS2 release, or use PCSX2 with a legally dumped copy.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster; Freedom 2 is a related portable entry, not a direct replacement.

entries.title: Monster Hunter Frontier

emulation.notes: Online service ended; revisit only if a legal archival route is sourced.

primary.why: Frontier was a Japan-only MMORPG that later updated through Frontier G and Frontier Z; the Windows route had the broadest update lineage, but the official service shut down in 2019.
primary.how_to_play: No current official play route; treat as preservation-only unless a legal server/archive route is sourced.

entries.remaster_caveats: Online service shut down on December 18, 2019.

emulation.notes: Use a legally dumped PSP copy.

primary.why: Freedom 2 is a PSP entry retaining and expanding on Monster Hunter 2 content; its enhanced sequel Freedom Unite is tracked separately.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PSP or use PPSSPP with a legally dumped copy.

emulation.notes: Use a legally dumped PSP copy.

primary.why: Freedom Unite is the enhanced version of Freedom 2; PSP via PPSSPP is the most stable preservation/high-fidelity route, while iOS availability is historically variable.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PSP or use PPSSPP with a legally dumped copy.

entries.title: Monster Hunter Tri

emulation.notes: Use a legally dumped Wii copy.

primary.how_to_play: Play the Wii version, or use Dolphin with a legally dumped copy.

entries.title: Monster Hunter Dynamic Hunting

emulation.notes: Use retained iOS install where available.

primary.how_to_play: Use a legally retained iOS copy/install if available.

entries.title: Monster Hunter: World

entries.remaster_caveats: For Master Rank expansion content, see Iceborne.
